explanation: erdosproblems.com/887: Erdős and Rosenfeld ask whether 4 is best possible for having infinitely many n with that many divisors in (√n, √n + C n^{1/4}). The Lean statement says 4 is not the greatest K for which some C > 0 admits infinitely many n with ≥ K such divisors, i.e. a negative answer, citing a forum construction (C = 31, five divisors, n = (x²−1)(x²−4)(x²−16)(x²−49) with z² = 56x² + 65) and a linked Lean proof. Reading 'best possible' as quantified over the constant C is the natural one, since for fixed C at most about C² + 1 divisors are possible. Faithful.
